claims.text: A WebSocket over HTTP/1.1 starts as an HTTP request asking to switch protocols; once the server accepts, the connection stays open and either the client or the server can send a message at any time.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core 10 docs: WebSockets support in ASP.NET Core; ADR 0032 @ stage-4 lines 19-20

claims.text: ADR 0032 header: nothing is built at stage-4; the repository has no Support service, endpoint or chat code; the design is in docs/design/support-chat-design-review.md.

ADR 0032 decides a separate service DonHang.Support following the golden path, with its own database donhang_support on server db like Notifications and Payments, using ASP.NET Core's built-in WebSocket support with no added library.
ASP.NET Core 10 includes WebSocket support in the shared framework (WebSockets middleware), so a server can accept WebSocket connections without adding a library.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core 10 docs: WebSockets support in ASP.NET Core (UseWebSockets)

claims.text: Above the Decision excerpt, ADR 0032 lists a chat module in DonHang.Api and its cost (connections held open for minutes share Pods, limits and canary releases with order taking); below it, it answers a teammate that this goes against driver 4; its context section defines WebSocket.
Each message is saved in PostgreSQL first (conversation, shop, sender), then sent to open connections; the saved row, not the delivery, is the record.
With several Pods, a Pod publishes each saved message to a Redis publish/subscribe channel and each Pod passes it to the connections it holds; Redis holds only copies, as redis.yaml says.

Redis Pub/Sub delivers a published message only to clients subscribed at that moment and does not store it (at-most-once); a subscriber cut off then never receives it. Unlike a RabbitMQ queue, a channel holds nothing.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: Pub/Sub, delivery semantics; RabbitMQ docs: Queues

claims.text: redis.yaml (kustomize base) comment: everything in Redis is a copy of what PostgreSQL holds, so losing it loses nothing that cannot be read again; the Deployment has replicas: 1.

On reconnecting, the app sends the id of its last message; the Pod reads newer messages from the database and sends them before new ones; a message during the drop is missed only on the Redis leg (driver 2).
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0032-... @ stage-4 line 45; docs/design/support-chat-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 53-56

claims.text: A reply unread after 5 minutes (assumed) becomes a message through the outbox, then RabbitMQ, and Notifications emails the customer under ADR 0027.

ADR 0032: shop taken from the access token, row-level security as ADR 0013; proposed endpoint /api/v1/conversations with a new HTTPRoute to Support; last two bullets cover rolling-update releases and the fallback.
httproutes.yaml at stage-4 sends /api/v1 (and /api/v2, /openapi) to Service api port 8080, and /api/v1/refunds to Service payments instead, because the longer path prefix wins.

Review deep dive (heading 'bước 4' = step 4 of system-design-method.md, the deep dive): a connection drops on a phone network or when a Pod is replaced in a release; the app reconnects after a wait with jitter so apps do not all reconnect at once.
Review: Redis (one replica) is a single point of failure for the relay between Pods only; losing it stops no saving or reading, and apps read missed messages on reconnect.
Review estimate: about 200 connections at the busy hour, about 1.7 messages per second, each one short write to donhang_support; with 2 Pods about 100 connections each (assumed).
Conversations and messages are owned by Support (data-ownership.md), per ADR 0032's consequences.

Deliver-then-save loses a message if the Pod stops between steps (fails driver 2); delivering only to own connections fails driver 1 with several Pods; the Redis relay is acceptable only because the saved row makes a miss recoverable.

claims.text: If Support ran one Pod, keep the channel when a second is planned; if Redis is down, driver 2 holds; nothing makes a healthy connection reconnect, so a missed reply shows after the app's next drop; reads go to donhang_support.
